lessons.trigger: When a structured-document review finds repealed or renumbered headings retained only as annotations, or a heading groups multiple section numbers,
lessons.guidance: Revise the section-record extraction so each required section number becomes its own articles object, while preserving shared source for grouped numbers. In this US Code case, the recipe used `mode: sections`, `heading_selector: h3.section-head`, and `start_pattern: ^§\s*\d+`; the review specifically suggests testing omitted `start_pattern` when all selected headings must become records, and `key_separator` to split grouped identifiers. Preview the revised output and confirm the flagged headings actually produce independent records before resubmitting.
lessons.avoid: Do not treat an annotation attached to a neighboring record as satisfying the independent-record requirement, or assume a recipe change fixed the output without checking the resulting objects. This evidence supports a repair direction, not a verified repair.

lessons.trigger: When inspecting an unfamiliar structured document and an initial selector returns `empty_selection`,
lessons.guidance: Use `document_inspect` without a selector for a structure inventory, then choose selectors based on observed tags and classes; for XML, use observed descendant tags with `.//Tag`.
lessons.avoid: Do not repeat the failed selector; selectors are case-sensitive, and the subsequent successful inspections here do not establish that the initial CSS selector was appropriate.

lessons.trigger: When section extraction from an HTML law puts chapter headings into an article body, and the source uses the same selected paragraph units for headings and article text
lessons.guidance: Use document_inspect to confirm the heading and article units, then revise document_preview in sections mode with an exclude_pattern for chapter headings (for example, ^第[一二三四五六七八九十百千〇零两0-9]+章), while retaining the article start/key patterns and collection_key="articles". Check the revised preview’s changed source paths and independent review before document_export; here the exclusion changed affected article text without changing the 82-record count and was accepted.
lessons.avoid: Do not use start_pattern to turn a chapter heading into a new article record. Excluding headings keeps them out of the articles collection, so separately verify that the requested output preserves needed structural material; do not infer completeness for other laws or requirements from this single accepted review.

Check the revised preview’s changed source paths and independent review before document_export; in the reviewed case, the exclusion changed affected article text without changing the 82-record count and was accepted.

lessons.trigger: When extracting U.S. Code sections from GovInfo HTML, where headings can group multiple section numbers and paragraphs use the class `note-body`.
lessons.guidance: Inspect the source structure with `document_inspect` (for example, `h3.section-head` and `p.note-body`) before designing the recipe. Exclude `note-body` from statutory body text only if the output actually moves that material into annotations. For grouped headings such as a repealed-section heading, use a splitting method that creates a separate article object for each observed section number while retaining their common source. Then use `document_preview` to verify both the generated objects and the body/annotation partition; an effective output change is not by itself evidence that the review findings are fixed.
lessons.avoid: Do not treat a grouped heading as a single record or leave it only as an adjacent record’s annotation when each section needs its own object. Do not assume `key_separator` works: here adding it changed no output, and `body_selector: p:not(.note-body)` changed output but did not resolve the grouped-heading finding. Stop rather than retry after the source repair budget is exhausted.

lessons.trigger: When a document review identifies a concrete recipe defect, and later inspection or review is blocked by a source limit.
lessons.guidance: Use the cited review finding and observed source values to plan a distinct next operation, then verify its actual output with the registered preview/review tools before claiming resolution. If inspection is blocked, report the saved limitation and leave the result incomplete rather than treating an unchanged retry or a recipe-only edit as recovery.
lessons.avoid: Do not repeat an inspection after `document_inspect` reports `recovery_action_required`; here the source was already at its inspection limit, and the subsequent `document_review` confirmed the repair budget was exhausted. Do not claim completion or retain unexecuted repair advice as a verified lesson.

lessons.trigger: When extracting numbered legal provisions from a source where chapter headings are selected alongside article paragraphs, and review finds a chapter heading embedded in an article body
lessons.guidance: Use document_inspect to confirm the selected source units, then revise the sections recipe with an exclude_pattern that identifies chapter headings while keeping the article start/key patterns intact. Re-run document_preview and compare the candidate output: verify the cited heading is removed from the article body, source paths/text actually change, and the independent review accepts the revised output before export. In the demonstrated CNIPA page, the recipe used selector and body_selector `div.article-content p`, collection_key `articles`, article pattern `^第[一二三四五六七八九十百千〇零两0-9]+条`, and excluded chapter headings with `^第[一二三四五六七八九十百千〇零两0-9]+章`.
lessons.avoid: Do not treat adding `collection_key: articles` as fixing content—the initial preview had the required key but review still found a chapter heading mixed into an article. Do not rely on unchanged record count as evidence that the repair had no effect; compare changed record fields, source paths, and actual output. A successful export or accepted structural review does not establish semantic accuracy beyond the review scope.

lessons.trigger: When extracting U.S. Code sections from govinfo HTML with `document_preview` in `sections` mode, especially where headings may group multiple section numbers or paragraphs include editorial history.
lessons.guidance: Before finalizing the recipe, inspect actual heading and paragraph classes with `document_inspect`. In the demonstrated source, editorial material uses `p.note-body`, while a grouped repealer is labeled `[§§155, 155A. Repealed.`. Configure `body_selector` to partition observed note paragraphs, and ensure the heading/start/key rules admit grouped-number headings. Then use `document_preview` to verify that the grouped heading yields one article per section with the same source, and that the actual article body and annotations are separated; compare output fields and record counts rather than treating a recipe change as proof of repair.
lessons.avoid: Do not assume `key_separator` fixes a grouped heading if the heading was filtered out by `start_pattern`; in this run adding `key_separator` changed no output. Do not assume excluding `.note-body` resolves all body/annotation mixing: the review still found a mix in the resulting record. Do not export an unaccepted candidate as complete.

lessons.trigger: When a document candidate has received specific negative review findings and a repair attempt produces no record-field or output-fingerprint change.
lessons.guidance: Use the cited findings to target the next preview operation: change the rule that admits and splits the grouped heading, and the selector partition that affects the reviewed body/annotation content. Confirm that the next `document_preview` changes the relevant records and then re-evaluate the findings. If the source’s repair budget is exhausted, stop retrying that source and report the saved limitation rather than treating repeated review calls as recovery.
lessons.avoid: Do not make cosmetic recipe changes that leave the output unchanged, or retry `document_review` after the recovery guard says the repair budget is exhausted. In this run, adding `key_separator` left the fingerprint and record count unchanged, and subsequent reviews were blocked.

limitations: Controlled numeric-prefix recipe is an operator-supplied failure; natural error frequency is not measured.
Both baseline and candidate pass the two independent document replay cases in all three controlled trials; no admission or persistent adoption is justified.
Unseeded tasks use known official URLs; this does not measure source discovery or confirm newest legal validity.
Within-task advice plus an output change is an observed sequence, not isolated causal improvement; no counterfactual controlled run was made for the natural repair.
Precursor trials used frozen earlier code and sometimes ran concurrently; their time differences are not an efficiency experiment.
Review, Reflector and Curator use the same service/model family; private source-specific post-run assertions remain separate from their inputs.
This engineering integration is not a reproduction of ACE benchmark performance.
